subject: Post-call: multiplexing & capacity clarification for FastCommerce POC
messages:
From: Kelly Zhang <kelly.zhang@fastcommerce.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Cc: John Li <john.li@fastcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-10-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + traffic profile (post-demo)

Thanks Ben — great walkthrough today. A couple things we promised to share and clarify on our side: we've attached a small CSV with our expected burst profile and a short note on streaming expectations. High level:
- Peak concurrent shoppers triggering AI assists: ~420 sessions
- Typical sustained concurrent inference requests during sale windows: 180-260
- Expected average request payload: 220 tokens in, streaming responses averaging 300 tokens out
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end token streaming experience < 250ms after first token

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) How does Redwood handle multiplexed parallel requests over a smallish connection pool (we can't open thousands of outbound sockets from our edge containers)?
2) What are your default rate-limit behaviors for the hosted API vs. dedicated capacity (burst windows)?
3) Any recommended connection pool size / keep-alive configs to avoid head-of-line blocking for streaming use-cases?

Attaching the CSV and a short load sketch. Can Ben / engineer set expectations for an async sizing calc? We'd like a written recommendation before our procurement team drafts PO.

--
Kelly Zhang
Director, Platform Engineering
FastCommerce

Attachments: 2028-10-11_FastCommerce_load_profile.csv (text/csv)
From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: Kelly Zhang <kelly.zhang@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-10-11T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + traffic profile (post-demo)

Kelly — thanks for the detailed profile and for joining the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood:

Recap (agreeing with your bullet points):
- Burst peak concurrent sessions: ~420, sustained 180-260
- Streaming responses, ~300 tokens out on average
- Latency target: p95 <250ms (we'll clarify what portion is network vs inference)

Immediate asks (we'll handle technical sizing):
- Rishi: can you run a small estimate using their CSV and our multiplexing model (assume 100ms per token on g5-class, quantized model path)? We need an expected GPU concurrency footprint and a recommended connection pool size for their edge containers.
- Marissa: I'll prepare a pricing sketch for two options — Hosted API with burst allowance and Redwood Dedicated minimal reserved pool — and call out expected rate-limit floors.

Notes on multiplexing + connection pools (short):
- Redwood supports persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive and HTTP/2 multiplexing on the hosted API; streaming via chunked transfer will stream tokens as they're generated.
- Default hosted-rate limits: 60 concurrent streams per API key and 1200 requests/min (soft); we can discuss raised soft-limits during POC.
- For your edge container constraint (small socket count): recommend connection pool of 40-60 sockets per service instance with HTTP/2 multiplexing enabled. That gives good parallelism without thousands of sockets while keeping head-of-line minimal.

Deliverables:
- Technical sizing estimate (Rishi) by EOD tomorrow
- Pricing/quote (Marissa) by Wednesday EOB
- Proposed MOP (mutual action plan) including an infra call for a quick load test during the POC window

I'll include our standard attachment describing multiplexing design — attaching a short PDF.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_mux_design_notes.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Kelly Zhang <kelly.zhang@fastcommerce.com>, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-10-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + traffic profile (post-demo)

Kelly — jumping in to outline the commercial options so expectations are aligned:

Option A — Hosted with elevated burst:
- Short-term: increase soft concurrency ceiling for POC to 600 concurrent streams (subject to fair-use and observed token throughput)
- Rate-limits: bump to 2500 requests/min for the POC window, with automatic fallback to standard limits outside of POC hours
- Pricing: usage-based with a surge premium during burst windows (we'll show worked example once Rishi shares the GPU-footprint estimate)

Option B — Dedicated (recommended if sustained traffic >200 concurrent for long periods):
- Reserved GPU pool mapped to expected peak. We typically size for 1.2x peak to allow for warm-up and leader-election events.
- Fixed monthly commitment + overage at lower per-token rate
- Can include a higher connection pool guarantee and SLA for p95 latency

Next steps: share the estimate and we'll send a one-page MSA addendum for the POC that captures temporary increased quotas and a target SLA. If procurement needs an exact PO template we can provide a doc.

Thanks — Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: Kelly Zhang <kelly.zhang@fastcommerce.com>, ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-10-12T11:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + traffic profile (post-demo)

Kelly / team — did a quick back-of-envelope using the CSV you provided (attached in-thread). Summary of assumptions and outcome:

Assumptions:
- Model inference latency: 0.09s/token (quantized path on g5x2 equivalent)
- Average response tokens: 300 => average generation time ~27s (but streaming means first token << 1s)
- Average concurrent inference per session during response window: 0.7 (not every active session generates at once)
- Network RTT: 40-60ms typical (we'll measure during load test)

Sizing outcome (sustained 220 concurrent):
- GPU concurrency needed: ~12 model instances (with batching) = ~3 x g5x2 nodes estimated (depends on batching targets).
- Recommended connection pool per edge instance: 48 sockets with HTTP/2 multiplexing. This keeps outstanding streams per socket ~6-8 during bursts.
- For bursts up to 420 concurrent: plan on 1.6x headroom => recommend Dedicated reserve with burst autoscale enabled, or hosted with guaranteed elevated soft-limits and pre-warmed pool.

Notes on rate-limits/quota:
- If you go hosted, we'll provision a POC quota increase (temporary) tied to the HubSpot deal. That increase won't change the production default; for production we recommend Dedicated.
- We will instrument a short workload test that measures p95 end-to-end token latency — that will let us split observed latency into network vs model-generation buckets and tune batching.

I'll pull together a compact sizing table and an ops checklist for the load test. Can you confirm which container images and region you'll run the load generator from?

-- Rishi
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kelly Zhang <kelly.zhang@fastcommerce.com>
